title: Call screening service
summary: Live rule evaluation on incoming calls, with real control over the outcome
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. WARNING — every API claim here is UNVERIFIED. No Android SDK on this machine. F001's task T002 must confirm these before this phase is planned in detail. Guidelines §4 forbids treating them as decided.

Implement android.telecom.CallScreeningService. It is believed to receive the incoming number at call time, so it calls F002's evaluate directly — all seven rule types, live, no expansion. This is the surface iOS cannot match.

ASSUMED RESPONSE CONTROLS (CallScreeningService.CallResponse): setDisallowCall, setRejectCall, setSilenceCall, setSkipCallLog, setSkipNotification. If correct, this answers what iOS cannot: whether a blocked call rings silently or is rejected, whether it appears in the call log, and whether a missed-call notification is shown. Expose these as user choices — it is real product value that only exists here.

ROLE: requires ROLE_CALL_SCREENING via RoleManager. Acquisition flow unverified and feeds R4's enablement screen.

PERFORMANCE: this runs on the call path. Evaluation must be fast and must not need the whole dataset loaded. Decide what happens if evaluation is slow or throws — failing open (letting the call through) is safer than failing closed, but must be deliberate.

ALSO VERIFY IN T002: whether BlockedNumberProvider is relevant, and its exact-number-only limitation.

FEEDS R6: the call screening service is what makes one-tap block from a received call possible here.
